articles.title: Fairbuds 2 : Fairphone abandonne son design arrondi pour des écouteurs à tige — Frandroid
articles.text:
La marque Fairphone est connue pour son engagement en faveur de la réparabilité. Elle préparerait la succession de ses écouteurs Fairbuds, lancés en avril 2024 alors que le casque Fairbuds XL sorti en 2025 est toujours disponible en rayon. D’après les clichés obtenus par NieuweMobiel, les Fairbuds 2 seraient en rupture avec le design des modèles précédents.
En effet, là où les Fairbuds originaux affichaient une forme ovale et arrondie, sans tige apparente, les Fairbuds 2 optent pour un design classique à tige, similaire à celui adopté par la majorité des écouteurs intra-auriculaires actuellement commercialisés.
Vers une plus grande autonomie ?
Le boîtier de charge évolue également. Les photos montrent un boîtier visiblement plus épais que celui du modèle précédent, ce qui peut laisser penser que la batterie serait plus grosse et pourrait ainsi apporter une autonomie supérieure.
Le boîtier repéré dans la fuite dispose par ailleurs d’un port USB-C, de points de contact métalliques destinés à la charge des écouteurs, ainsi que de LED de statut placées en son centre.
Deux coloris ont été identifiés sur les visuels : un vert baptisé Forest Green et un noir baptisé Horizon Black. Ces deux teintes reprennent exactement les coloris du smartphone Fairphone 6 Plus, récemment commercialisé par la marque.
La réparabilité en question
L’argument central des Fairbuds, c’est la réparabilité, fer de lance de la marque. Selon le fabricant, sept pièces différentes pouvaient être remplacées par l’utilisateur lui-même à l’aide d’un simple tournevis cruciforme et d’un outil de levier : les batteries de chaque écouteur, la batterie du boîtier, les bagues et embouts en silicone, ainsi que la coque extérieure du boîtier. Cette approche avait valu aux Fairbuds une note maximale de réparabilité auprès d’iFixit, référence en la matière.
    Pour aller plus loin
            Test des Fairphone Fairbuds : des écouteurs éco-responsables et réparables
            
Selon toute vraisemblance, les Fairbuds 2 resteront modulaires, mais Fairphone n’a pour l’instant précisé aucune pièce remplaçable concernant cette nouvelle génération. Le changement de design pose justement la question du maintien de cette promesse. La plupart des écouteurs à tige disponibles sur le marché intègrent des batteries collées à l’intérieur du boîtier, une solution technique permettant de gagner de la place mais rendant le remplacement impossible sans intervention spécialisée.
Cependant, sur les visuels, on peut voir une ligne de jonction visible entre la tige et le corps de l’écouteur ce qui pourrait indiquer que la tige elle-même propose une partie détachable.
La qualité audio sera-t-elle de mise ?
Sur le plan technique, les Fairbuds originaux proposaient des transducteurs de 11 mm à revêtement titane, une réduction de bruit active complétée d’une réduction du bruit du vent, six microphones, une connectivité Bluetooth 5.3 avec fonction multipoint, une certification IP54 contre l’eau et la transpiration, ainsi qu’une autonomie totale annoncée de 26 heures avec le boîtier de charge. Nous verrons sur les remplaçants suivent cette logique.
Fairphone dévoilera les caractéristiques complètes, les pièces remplaçables et le prix des Fairbuds 2 lors de leur lancement, attendu au quatrième trimestre 2026.

articles.title: OpenAI entrenó GPT-6 Astra con 100.000 GPUs: Nvidia prevé que el próximo modelo de IA necesitará 400.000
articles.text:
OpenAI, la empresa de Sam Altman, entrenó GPT-6 Astra con 100.000 tarjetas gráficas en el centro de datos Stargate de Abilene, Texas, Estados Unidos, una operación cuyo costo operativo se estima entre 500 millones y 1.000 millones de dólares y que según Jensen Huang, CEO de Nvidia, anticipa una expansión de cuatro veces esa escala para el próximo modelo de inteligencia artificial (IA).
El entrenamiento se prolongó entre 90 y 120 días. La estimación de costos parte de un valor de entre 2,50 y 3,50 dólares por hora para cada procesador gráfico utilizado durante ese período continuo.
PUBLICIDAD
La futura infraestructura podría requerir cerca de 1,2 GW de potencia eléctrica si se construye con 400.000 GPU y bastidores GB200 NVL72 de Nvidia. Esa cifra incluye un factor de eficiencia energética de 1,5, que contempla la electricidad adicional destinada a refrigeración y otros sistemas del centro de datos.
Cómo fue diseñado GPT-6 Astra, el nuevo modelo de OpenAI
GPT-6 Astra fue diseñado para utilizar herramientas externas sin que los desarrolladores deban programar una interfaz de programación de aplicaciones, conocida como API, para cada una de ellas. El sistema puede actuar de manera similar a un usuario que interactúa con programas informáticos.
PUBLICIDAD
Sus agentes se desplazan por navegadores web, hojas de cálculo y aplicaciones de escritorio. Con esa capacidad, pueden elaborar documentos completos, diseñar presentaciones y resolver secuencias de trabajo complejas.
La base de razonamiento funciona mediante una arquitectura nativa de múltiples agentes. Ante una tarea de alta dificultad, un agente principal plantea una hipótesis técnica y coordina a subagentes independientes que prueban alternativas y verifican resultados en paralelo.
PUBLICIDAD
Esa distribución de tareas busca evitar los llamados “bucles de perdición”, momentos en las que un modelo queda atrapado en intentos repetitivos sin resolver un problema. Permite que el modelo depure su propio código y modifique su estrategia cuando identifica fallas.
Sin embargo, la dimensión del despliegue no implica un liderazgo automático en todas las evaluaciones. El modelo Fable 5.1 de Anthropic supera a Astra en pruebas técnicas estandarizadas como SWE-bench Pro, Artificial Analysis Intelligence, Coding Agent y ProofBench v1.1, dedicado a problemas matemáticos formales.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuál es la previsión de Nvidia ante la llegada de nuevos modelos
Jensen Huang exaltó a OpenAI tras la puesta en marcha de Astra y adelantó una próxima etapa de entrenamiento con 400.000 tarjetas gráficas operando en simultáneo. Huang sostuvo que la inteligencia artificial general, o AGI, ya llegó.
Ese volumen cuadruplicaría las más de 100.000 GPU utilizadas para Astra y podría ocupar la totalidad del complejo Stargate en Texas. La previsión no incluye una fecha para el inicio del nuevo entrenamiento ni detalla cuánto tiempo demandaría.
PUBLICIDAD
La estimación eléctrica se basa en bastidores NVIDIA GB200 NVL72, con un consumo aproximado de 140 kW cada uno. Entonces, para alojar 400.000 GPU serían necesarios unos 5.555,55 bastidores bajo esa configuración.
Asimismo, la multiplicación de esa cantidad de estructuras por su consumo y por el factor de eficiencia energética lleva la demanda hasta los 1,2 GW. No obstante, la cifra solo es una hipótesis sobre la potencia necesaria para completar el entrenamiento. No confirma que toda la infraestructura vaya a usar exactamente esos servidores.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué problemas ha tenido el lanzamiento de Astra al público
El lanzamiento del modelo GPT-6 Astra de OpenAI ha tenido errores de acceso inicial, porque los usuarios de pago de ChatGPT no pudieron usar el sistema poco después de su lanzamiento. Su director ejecutivo, Sam Altman, tuvo que pedir disculpas y afirmó que el lanzamiento había sido “un desastre”.
El jefe de OpenAI reconoció en X: “En primer lugar, perdón por el lanzamiento desastroso”. Agregó: “En segundo lugar, cuando metemos la pata, intentamos arreglarlo”.

articles.title: Cloudflare Tests Cache Transcoding to Reduce Storage Requirements
articles.text:
Cloudflare recently described a prototype called Cache Transcoding that compresses eligible cache content, mainly uncompressed text such as HTML, JSON, CSS, and JavaScript, using Zstandard before storing it on disk. The hyperscaler estimates that the approach could provide petabytes of additional effective cache capacity, although broader testing is still needed.
According to the article, the additional processing required is relatively small, as the content is compressed once when it enters the cache and decompressed when served. Compression reduced the size of eligible content by about 2.8 times, allowing existing servers to store more data and reducing the amount of data transferred between data centers.
To achieve this, Cloudflare relies on Zstandard, the lossless compression algorithm developed by Facebook for real-time use, together with Pingora, its Rust-based proxy framework. Aashi Patel writes:
A small increase in CPU gives Cloudflare petabytes of effective cache capacity and reduces the data transferred between our data centers. The encoding cost is paid once when an asset enters the cache. The storage and bandwidth savings continue every single time that asset is reused.
Cloudflare's Cache Transcoding only compresses uncompressed responses that contain compressible text, return successfully, and are at least 4 KiB. It excludes range requests, precompressed or binary content, and responses with an unknown size. The threshold avoids processing many small objects while sacrificing only about 1% of eligible data, and both this threshold and the Zstandard compression level can be adjusted based on CPU and storage trade-offs. Patel adds:
Transcoding does not mean compressing everything. Images, video, and fonts are usually compressed already. In our traffic sample, this media slice represented 21.4% of requests but 63.3% of bytes. Compressing it again would burn CPU for nothing.
According to Cloudflare, compressible text such as HTML, JSON, CSS, and JavaScript accounted for 67.3% of requests and 22.3% of bytes. Of this content, about 71% arrived uncompressed and could be effectively compressed.
Source: Cloudflare blog
While some practitioners question the use of the word "transcoding" for an encode/decode approach, others on Hacker News discuss the compression options. As Cloudflare initially considered limiting transcoding to popular content, user MayeulC writes:
Weird, I would have compressed cold content instead, if the goal was to save on CPU time during decode.
User CodesInChaos asks instead:
I'm confused by how this affects range requests. Without compression, those can be easily satisfied by reading the relevant part of the cached complete file. But how are they handled now?
Tests were performed with and without Tiered Cache to measure the impact of compression on local caching and transfers between cache tiers. The prototype remains under development, with further testing planned across different compression levels, content types, object sizes, and cache scenarios.

articles.title: AZZA PSAZ-750G ATX 3.1 power supply review: An adequate budget 750W unit
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Helly-built PSAZ-750G measures like a decent budget Gold-class unit and is priced like one, but the 80 PLUS Gold badge on the box is not backed by any certification, and our own numbers put it just under the Gold threshold at half load. Add a 2-year warranty, hardwired cables and a 450W-limited 12V-2x6, and the $78 asking price stops looking generous.
Pros
- +Aggressive $78 price
- +Solid 12V regulation
- +Genuine fanless window
- +Native 12V-2x6 connector
- +Compact 140 mm chassis
- +Ball bearing fan
Cons
- -Uncertified 80 PLUS badge
- -Only 2-year warranty
- -450W limited 12V-2x6
- -Loud when hot
- -Low-grade capacitors
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
AZZA is one of those brands that has been around far longer than its shelf presence suggests. The company is the PC-components arm of Linkworld Electronic, and it has spent the better part of two decades selling cases, coolers, chassis fans and power supplies into the value end of the market, mostly through regional distribution rather than the big review-sample circuit. That low profile cuts both ways. AZZA has never had the marketing budget to overpromise the way larger brands do, but it also has never had to answer for its power supplies in public the way brands like Corsair or Cooler Master routinely do. Like almost every brand in this segment, AZZA designs none of their units themselves but buys platforms from (usually Chinese) OEMs and puts its own sticker on the side.
The PSAZ series is AZZA's mainstream ATX line, and the PSAZ-750G is the 750W Gold-badged member of it. The unit we have is marked ATX 3.1 and PCIe 5.1 Ready on the box, carries a native 12V-2x6 connector, and is rated for its full 750W at 40°C ambient. It ships with a 2-year warranty, which is a statement all by itself. The platform comes from Helly, a manufacturer that supplies a number of platforms and we meet their products frequently in mainstream units. What makes the PSAZ-750G interesting is not the specification sheet but the badge on it: the box, the label and the retail listings all carry the 80 PLUS Gold logo, and AZZA has not put a PSAZ unit through 80 PLUS certification since 2015. That claim, more than anything else, is what this review has to settle and determine whether it deserves a spot in our list of best power supplies.
Specifications and Design
| AZZA PSAZ-750G ATX 3.1 Power specifications ( Rated @ 40 °C ) |  |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RAIL | +3.3V | +5V | +12V | +5Vsb | -12V | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAX OUTPUT | 20A | 20A | 62A | 2.5A | 0.3A | 
| Row 1 - Cell 0 | 100W | 100W | 744W | 12.5W | 3.6W | 
| TOTAL | 750W | Row 2 - Cell 2 | Row 2 - Cell 3 | Row 2 - Cell 4 | Row 2 - Cell 5 | 
| AC INPUT | 100 - 240 VAC, 50 - 60 Hz | Row 3 - Cell 2 | Row 3 - Cell 3 | Row 3 - Cell 4 | Row 3 - Cell 5 | 
| MSRP | $78 | Row 4 - Cell 2 | Row 4 - Cell 3 | Row 4 - Cell 4 | Row 4 - Cell 5 | 
In the Box
Packaging is plain and inexpensive, and honest about it. The sleeve is a flat slate-blue with the AZZA wordmark rendered as three large outlined chevrons on the left, a line drawing of the unit on the right, and the model and wattage stacked underneath. The badges run along the lower half - PCI-e 5.1 Ready, ATX 3.1, and the 80 PLUS Gold logo in its usual gold square. The unit sits inside between two moulded protective inserts, with the cables bundled beside it.
The bundle is as thin as it gets. There is the AC power cord, four mounting screws and four black zip ties. No Velcro straps, no cable combs, no pouch, no tester, and nothing in the way of printed documentation beyond what is on the box itself. At $78 for a 750W unit, none of that is unreasonable, but it is worth noting that the four zip ties are doing real work here. With a hardwired cable set there is no way to leave unused cables out of the case, so whatever routing tidiness you get, you will be building yourself.
The cables themselves are better than the accessory list implies. All of them are black nylon-sleeved rather than the flat ribbon type common at this price, sleeved right up to the connector housings, and the wire gauges look appropriate throughout. The 12V-2x6 cable is a native run from the PCB rather than an adapter, and it is printed with a 450W rating along its length, which is the single most important thing to know about this power supply before you buy it. That is enough for a mid-range card, and not enough for a 500W+ flagship, regardless of what the 750W on the box suggests. There is no dual-color keying on the connector, so seating it correctly is on you.
| AZZA PSAZ-750G ATX 3.1 |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Connector type | Hardwired | Modular | 
| ATX 24 Pin | 1 | - | 
| EPS 4+4 Pin | 2 | - | 
| EPS 8 Pin | - | - | 
| PCI-E 5.1 | 1 | - | 
| PCI-E 8 Pin | 3 | - | 
| SATA | 6 | - | 
| Molex | 2 | - | 
| Floppy | - | - | 
External Appearance
At 150 x 86 x 140 mm the PSAZ-750G is a standard-depth ATX unit, and 140 mm means it drops into essentially any case that takes an ATX supply, with enough clearance left over to deal with the fixed cable loom. The chassis is finished in a dark grey-brown matte paint and it is a better finish than the price would predict. The top face carries a slotted grille with wide diagonal bars over the fan, cut off at one corner by a plain triangular panel bearing the AZZA logo and a few thin pinstripes. It is a restrained, slightly industrial look, and the diagonal grille bars do restrict airflow area more than a wire or honeycomb grille would, which increases noise.
The side panel carries the only color on the unit: a grey hatched rectangle with the AZZA wordmark in outline and 750W set in a bright cyan that matches the box. The top side holds the specifications label, and it is worth reading. It lists the ATX 3.1 and PCIe 5.1 Ready marks and, again, the 80 PLUS Gold logo.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The rear face is a hexagonal honeycomb exhaust panel with the AC receptacle, the main I/O rocker, and a second, smaller square button beside it. That button is the hybrid fan mode switch: press it and the semi-passive behavior is disabled, so the fan runs continuously from idle rather than waiting for load. It is a feature several units at three times this price still omit, and it is faintly odd to find it here. The front face is solid, with the fixed cable loom leaving through a single rubber-grommeted opening. There is no modular bay, no LED, and no other features.
Internal Design
Cooling comes from a 120 mm Yate Loon D12BH-12, a ball-bearing fan rated at 12V and 0.60A. Yate Loon publishes this model at 2300 RPM, 89 CFM and 41 dB(A) at full speed, which puts it firmly in the high-airflow, high-noise half of the catalogue. Ball bearings are a durability advantage over the sleeve-bearing fans that usually appear at this price, and given the 2-year warranty that matters - a fan that outlasts the coverage period is the minimum bar. What it is not is a quiet fan, and the platform leans on it hard, as the hot-box results below make clear.
The platform is a Helly design and is similar to the platform Phanteks AMP GH series is using - but that is where the similarities end. The layout is clean and reasonably modern, with the main PCB carrying the primary and secondary stages and a pair of small vertical daughterboards near the front handling the minor rails. Heatsinks are generously sized for the class, dark-anodised finned extrusions rather than the bent aluminium strips that budget platforms often make do with, and the board is well populated with silicone glue on the taller components. The main transformer is marked ATX3.0 on the bobbin, which is a small reminder of how recent the 3.1 revision on the box actually is.
Transient filtering runs to four Y capacitors, three X capacitors and two common-mode chokes, which is a complete filter by any reasonable standard and better provisioned than several units we have looked at this year. Inrush is handled by an NTC thermistor with a relay for bypass. Two bridge rectifiers sit on their own dedicated heatsink, feeding an APFC stage built around two Oriental Semiconductor OSG55R190F MOSFETs. The bulk capacitor is a 560 µF, 420V Ltec from its HP series, rated at 105°C. That is a low-cost Taiwanese part rather than a premium one, and it is the first place the budget shows. Capacity is adequate for 750W, the temperature rating is right, but the pedigree is not. The APFC coil beside is unshielded, which is a cost decision rather than a functional problem, though it does nothing for radiated noise.
The primary inversion stage uses two PIP PTA25N50 MOSFETs in a half-bridge LLC resonant arrangement, the standard modern topology at this power level. On the secondary side, the 12V rail is rectified by four Fuxin FXN0204C MOSFETs in synchronous rectification, with the 3.3V and 5V rails generated by DC-to-DC converters on the two vertical daughterboards.
Secondary filtering is a mix of Ltec electrolytics and a smaller number of APAQ polymer capacitors, both Taiwanese. This is the part of the component list that will decide how the unit ages: Ltec electrolytics are not terrible parts, but they are at best ordinary ones, and they will spend their life sitting next to secondary heatsinks that may hit well over 70 °C in a normal system. A 2-year warranty against that combination is not a comfortable pairing.
Cold Test Results (25°C Ambient)
Cold Test Results (25°C Ambient)
For the testing of PSUs, we are using high-precision electronic loads with a maximum power draw of 2700 Watts, a Rigol DS5042M 40 MHz oscilloscope, an Extech 380803 power analyzer, two high-precision UNI-T UT-325 digital thermometers, an Extech HD600 SPL meter, a self-designed hotbox, and various other bits and parts.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
At 25°C ambient the PSAZ-750G averaged 90.6% at 230 VAC and 88.6% at 115 VAC across the nominal load range. The curve peaks at about 92% at 230 VAC around 300W and holds 90.2% at a sustained 750W, with the 115 VAC line topping out at 90.3% and finishing at 87.3%. Those are respectable numbers and the shape of the curve is healthy, with no full-load collapse. They are also, and this is the point, not Gold. 80 PLUS Gold requires 90/92/89% at 20/50/100% load on 230 VAC and 87/90/87% on 115 VAC. We measured 90.1/91.8/90.2% and 88.7/89.9/87.1% respectively. The unit clears the 20% and 100% checkpoints on both inputs and misses the 50% checkpoint on both, by 0.2 and 0.1 points. It is a near miss rather than a fraud and CLEAResult tests at 23 °C so it could possibly pass, but there is no 80 PLUS entry for the PSAZ series after 2015 to argue otherwise. There is no Cybenetics listing either.
Acoustically the cold run is the best part of this review. The fan stays completely stopped up to roughly 40% load, giving a genuine 300W fanless window that covers desktop work and a good deal of gaming outright. It starts at 31.6 dB(A) and ramps gently to about 33 dB(A) at half load, at which point it becomes the quietest thing in most builds. Past 450W the curve steepens noticeably, reaching 38 dB(A) at 600W and 42 dB(A) at a sustained 750W. That is audible but not intrusive, and it is a reasonable trade for a good thermal result. The heatsinks reached 66-68°C at full load. Nothing here is under severe stress.
Hot Test Results (~45°C Ambient)
Hot Test Results (~45°C Ambient)
Inside the hotbox at roughly 45°C ambient, five degrees above the unit's own 40°C rating, efficiency falls by roughly a point and a half. It was not an unexpected result but it is severe for a 750W unit. The averages come to 89.4% at 230 VAC and 87.5% at 115 VAC, with the curve peaking near 90.8% and finishing at 88.5% and 85.6% respectively at full load. Nothing in the electrical behavior suggests the platform is in deep trouble but we can see the signs of thermal degradation at full load.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The thermal and acoustic picture is where the platform shows its limits. The fan leaves its passive mode in the hot box very quickly, starting at about 33.6 dB(A) from 200W, then climbing steeply and continuously: 43 dB(A) at 500W, 48.6 dB(A) at 600W, and 52.2 dB(A) at a sustained 750W. That last figure is loud in the plain sense of the word, well past the point where the PSU is the loudest component in a mid-tower and into the range where it likely is the loudest thing in the room. It is also the fan doing exactly what it should, because the internal temperatures need it. The heatsinks reached 94°C at full load, which is on the high side for a 750W unit. Those are not typically failure temperatures, but they are high enough to matter for the Ltec secondary electrolytics sitting beside them over a several-year ownership period.
PSU Quality and Bottom Line
Power Supply Quality
Voltage regulation is the strongest result on the sheet. Across the 20% to 100% load span the 12V rail moved by just 0.9%, with the 3.3V and 5V rails both at 1.4%. Sub-1% on 12V is genuinely good, better than several other Gold units, and it is the credit side of the DC-to-DC secondary arrangement. The minor rails are looser, but both stay comfortably inside the ±5% ATX window and neither matters much to a modern system.
Ripple suppression is adequate rather than good. The 12V rail peaked at 52 mV at full load and 50 mV in the 12V-weighted cross-load test, against a 120 mV ATX limit. The 3.3V and 5V rails topped out at 26 and 28 mV against their 50 mV limits. Those are passes with about 57% headroom on 12V and roughly 45% on the minor rails, so nothing is close to the edge. They are also roughly double what a well-filtered enthusiast platform delivers, and the 12V figure more than doubles between 50% and 100% load, which points at secondary filtering that is sized to the requirement rather than beyond it. For the hardware a 750W unit at this price will actually feed, it is sufficient.
During our thorough assessment, we evaluate the essential protection features of every power supply unit we review, including Over Current Protection (OCP), Over Voltage Protection (OVP), Over Power Protection (OPP), and Short Circuit Protection (SCP).
All protection mechanisms were present and triggered correctly. With the unit hot, OCP tripped at 146% on the 3.3V rail (29.2A), 140% on the 5V rail (28A), and 128% on the 12V rail (79.4A), with OPP shutting the unit down at about 130% of rated output, or roughly 975W. The 12V threshold is the sensible one of the three. The minor-rail thresholds are loose enough that the 100W combined budget is the real constraint there, not the protection.

Bottom Line
The PSAZ-750G is a competent budget power supply carrying a claim it cannot support. The Helly platform underneath is more modern than the price suggests and used by several manufacturers at this price point. Inside, we have a half-bridge LLC primary, DC-to-DC minor rails, a complete transient filter, generously sized heatsinks, a ball-bearing fan and a native 12V-2x6 connector. Regulation on the 12V rail is genuinely good at 0.9%, ripple is comfortably inside specification everywhere, protections all work and trip at sane thresholds, and the 300W fanless window at room temperature is real. There is nothing broken here.
The efficiency claim, however, is one that does not survive contact with the bench. Our numbers put the unit 0.2 points under the Gold requirement at 50% load on 230 VAC and 0.1 under it on 115 VAC, clearing every other checkpoint. CLEAResult tests at 23°C, so a good sample could plausibly clear the bar on the official bench. On the other hand, other units using the same platform passed our testing, even if they were fully modular (typically hardwired cables increase efficiency slightly). AZZA has not certified a PSAZ unit since 2015, there is no official 80 PLUS entry for this particular model, no Cybenetics listing and no PLPP listing, yet the Gold logo is printed on the box, on the label and in the retail listings. The unit performs like a borderline Gold supply. It is being sold as a certified one. Those are not the same thing, and the second is the vendor's choice, not a measurement artifact.
Most of the remaining compromises are ordinary for the money. Hardwired cabling at 750W in 2026 is behind the market but forgivable at $78, but the Ltec capacitors is what a $78 budget buys. One thing is harder to wave through. That is the 2-year warranty, which is half or less of what every serious competitor offers; set against heatsinks that reached 94°C at full load in the hot box, with ordinary electrolytics sitting beside them, it reads as the manufacturer telling you how long it expects the unit to be its problem.
Against named rivals, the placement is straightforward. The Phanteks AMP GH series runs a related Helly platform, which is worth keeping in mind - the design itself is not the problem here; the specification is. The MSI MAG A750GL PCIE5 is fully modular, genuinely 80 PLUS Gold certified, and backed by a 10-year warranty, and it is better than the AZZA on every axis except price. The Cooler Master MWE Gold 750 V4 at $119 MSRP is quieter under sustained load, carries verified Gold efficiency and a 10-year warranty, and gives up only a little on 12V regulation, where the AZZA's 0.9% is the better figure.
The PSAZ-750G beats them on nothing but cost, but it beats them there by a wide margin. So the recommendation is narrow but real. If you are building a mid-range machine on a tight budget, the card you are pairing it with draws under 450W, and you can live with 2 years of coverage and a fixed cable loom, the PSAZ-750G will do the job, and it will do it quietly at the loads you will actually run. If any of those three conditions do not hold, the extra money for a certified, longer-warrantied, fully modular unit is the better spend, and it is not a close call. Buy it for what it measures, not for the badge on the box.

articles.title: 5 películas y series con 100% en Rotten Tomatoes que puedes ver ahora mismo en Netflix
articles.text:
Netflix suele ser criticada por la baja calidad de sus películas. Pero durante este año, la plataforma ha puesto interés y esfuerzo en que su catálogo sea mucho más atractivo. Claro está, la discusión sobre la calidad de las producciones originales de Netflix es uno de los debates más complejos del mundo del entretenimiento. Porque, si bien la compañía brinda visibilidad a todo tipo de producciones que de otra forma no hubiesen llegado al gran público, tiene un problema. Que no todos los estrenos cumplen el estándar básico para ser proyectos de renombre dentro de la cultura pop actual.
Eso se debe a que la plataforma adapta una estrategia de volumen versus prestigio. A saber: su catálogo alberga simultáneamente producciones de consumo rápido y auténticas obras maestras aclamadas por la crítica. Esta dualidad permite que convivan fenómenos de audiencias con largometrajes y series galardonadas en los festivales de cine más prestigiosos del mundo. También, nominadas a los Premios Óscar y Emmy. Algo que hace complicado decidir qué ver y, sobre todo, qué escoger para pasar un rato divertido. ¿Una serie o película sin mucha calidad pero entretenida? ¿Una obra de calidad, pero que te costará encontrar?
Para solucionar ese inconveniente, uno de los métodos habituales es el de explorar en los agregadores de calificación crítica. El más importante y relevante, por supuesto, Rotten Tomatoes. Lo que permite tener una buena idea de qué producciones valen la pena y cuáles quizás es mejor apartar para otro momento. Si pasas mucho tiempo en ese proceso un poco engorroso, esta lista es para ti. Te dejamos 5 producciones con 100 % de críticas positivas en la página, todas estrenadas este año y disponibles en Netflix. De true crime a series de comedia, pasando por exploraciones sobre la naturaleza humana. Una selección especial para los que disfrutan de la calidad.
Confía en mí: El falso profeta
Esta impactante miniserie documental de Netflix tiene 100 % de aprobación crítica en Rotten Tomatoes y razones no faltan. Dirigida por un equipo de realizadoras nominadas al Emmy, funciona como la sucesora espiritual del éxito Sé dócil: Reza y obedece. Por lo que se adentra en una peligrosa investigación encubierta dentro de una secta polígama en la frontera de Utah y Arizona. Pero antes de solo ser una reconstrucción de los hechos, es también una reflexión acerca del motivo mismo de la existencia de sectas religiosas semejantes. Mucho más, la forma en que proliferan en la actualidad.
Para eso, la trama sigue a expertos que se infiltran para desenmascarar a un autoproclamado profeta moderno. Por lo que expone crímenes sistémicos y abuso de menores que culminan en una redada del FBI. A medida que los capítulos avanzan, la investigación inicial da un giro sumamente oscuro y desgarrador para los involucrados. Por lo que comienza como un análisis sociológico de las creencias de la secta, se vuelve más retorcido. Eso, al indagar en el descubrimiento de una red sistémica de explotación humana, manipulación de masas y abusos institucionales profundamente arraigados.
De modo que la miniserie termina por enfocarse en el drama humano de las víctimas. Para eso, recurre a testimonios íntimos de los supervivientes y, en especial, al horror que deben soportar tanto dentro como una vez fuera de la secta. Todo, a través de un meticuloso trabajo de campo de los investigadores. Para los amantes de los true crime de alto impacto y mejor calidad.
Una tóxica historia de amor
Otra de las producciones con 100 % de aprobación crítica en Rotten Tomatoes es este durísimo documental. Y razones sobran: el documental toma un inquietante caso de acoso cibernético para mostrar los alcances del maltrato doméstico. Pero más allá de eso, enfoca su atención en un hecho inquietante. Los blancos legales que abusadores y agresores pueden utilizar en su beneficio. Mucho más retorcido: la manera en que las diversas plataformas pueden ser el vehículo directo para el control y el maltrato.
Para eso, sigue el caso real de Ian y Angela Diaz. Esta, una pareja residente de California cuya idílica vida matrimonial se transforma rápidamente en una auténtica pesadilla. Todo debido a lo que parece ser un implacable acoso cibernético. Poco después de casarse y anunciar públicamente que esperaban gemelos, Angela comenzó a recibir correos electrónicos aterradores con amenazas explícitas de violencia y muerte. La situación escaló a niveles alarmantes cuando el acosador anónimo utilizó anuncios clasificados en internet para contratar a hombres desconocidos. Dándoles, además, la orden específica de acudir a la vivienda de la pareja para abusar sexualmente de la mujer.
Todas las sospechas de la policía y las víctimas recayeron de inmediato sobre Michelle Hadley, la exnovia de Ian. Una mujer en apariencia despechada, obsesiva y sumamente peligrosa. En medio de la amenaza, Michelle fue encarcelada. Solo para que después el caso diera un impactante giro. Las pruebas técnicas revelaron la escalofriante verdad. La propia Angela Diaz había orquestado minuciosamente todo el complot desde el principio. Todo con la intención de incriminar de manera perversa a Michelle mediante identidades falsas, manipulación psicológica y un elaborado engaño cibernético. Un caso aterrador que este documental cuenta a detalle y que ya puedes ver en Netflix.
El libro para colorear
Llega con retraso al catálogo de Netflix España, pero es otra brillante producción con 100 % de aprobación crítica en Rotten Tomatoes. Y eso por su capacidad para conmover y reflexionar filosóficamente sobre la vida en una misma historia. Dirigida por David Fortune, la cinta explora las profundidades del duelo, la paternidad y la resiliencia humana. La trama sigue a Lucky (William Catlett), un padre devoto que acaba de quedar viudo y debe aprender a reconstruir su existencia. Todo mientras cría en solitario a su hijo Mason, un encantador niño que tiene síndrome de Down.
Tras la dolorosa pérdida de la esposa y madre, la frágil estabilidad de este pequeño núcleo familiar se tambalea por la tristeza y la incertidumbre del futuro. Sin embargo, en medio del desgarrador vacío emocional, un amigo cercano les regala entradas para un partido de béisbol de los Atlanta Braves. El deseo del pequeño Mason de asistir al Truist Park se convierte en el motor que impulsa a ambos a salir de su aislamiento. También, romper la inercia de la depresión doméstica.
Por lo que la aventura se transforma en un profundo y transformador viaje espiritual para padre e hijo. La travesía pondrá a prueba la paciencia del padre, desatará las emociones reprimidas de ambos y les llevará a conocerse mejor. Lo que les servirá como un emotivo lienzo para retratar la infinita capacidad de superación. Ideal para los amantes de los dramas de calidad que puedes ver ahora mismo en Netflix.
Los superfrikis
Una rareza que puede presumir del 100 % de amor crítico en Rotten Tomatoes. Parte del siempre en crecimiento catálogo de Corea del Sur de la plataforma, la serie es ideal para los amantes del género de superhéroes que buscan algo distinto. En especial, porque esta refrescante propuesta de acción y comedia de superhéroes ambientada a finales del siglo pasado se burla de todos los clichés. También tiene un divertido y retorcido sentido del humor que logra explorar en el mundo de los héroes, pero sin caer en sentimentalismos.
Para eso, la serie se enfoca en la ficticia localidad de Haeseong en el año 1999. Sí, justo en pleno auge de la histeria colectiva por el temido efecto Y2K. En este particular contexto, un grupo de carismáticos pero desastrosos frikis adquiere accidentalmente extraños e inestables superpoderes tras un incidente químico corporativo. Por lo que se ven obligados a trabajar en equipo para detener una conspiración que amenaza su pacífico hogar.
Pero más extraño todavía, tratar de lidiar con su nueva vida como superhéroes, que claro está, no se parece en absoluto a la que habían soñado. Por lo que la serie es mucho más que una historia de personas peculiares en situaciones extraordinarias. También es un relato divertidísimo acerca de la búsqueda de la identidad y hasta de entender el valor de uno mismo. Un punto interesante que la serie lleva a un siguiente nivel en su (por ahora) única temporada.
Chris y Martina: El set decisivo
Otro 100 % en Rotten Tomatoes para completar la lista. Este extraordinario largometraje documental deportivo dirigido por Rebecca Gitlitz es ideal para los amantes del tenis. Y eso debido a que la producción se sumerge en las trayectorias paralelas de Chris Evert y Martina Navratilova. Estas dos leyendas indiscutibles dominaron la escena del tenis femenino durante las décadas de los setenta y ochenta. Por lo que la cinta relata la rivalidad más grande en la historia de este deporte, enfrentándose en ochenta partidos oficiales. Un largo recorrido que transformó por completo la percepción de las atletas mujeres ante las masas.
Para eso, el guion utiliza una impresionante recopilación de imágenes de archivo inéditas y transmisiones televisivas clásicas de torneos de Grand Slam. También, valiosas entrevistas exclusivas con figuras como Billie Jean King. Al inicio, la obra retrata el marcado contraste de sus personalidades. Por un lado, la elegancia de la estadounidense frente a la fuerza atlética de la checoslovaca. Este dinámico choque deportivo no solo generó tensiones emocionales profundas. También las empujó mutuamente hacia la excelencia competitiva, poniéndolas en un pedestal dorado que cambió el tenis profesional para siempre. Una historia que puedes disfrutar ahora mismo en Netflix.

articles.title: 'We're really doubling down on darkness' say Diablo 5 devs, and 'desolation is the setting for the story'
articles.text:
- Devs say that they're "really doubling down on darkness" with Diablo 5's setting
- This will build on Diablo 4's bleakness and darkness
- And continue to contrast the relative vibrancy of Diablo 3
After the somewhat vibrancy of Diablo 3 that some fans raised an eyebrow at, the bleak darkness and misery of Diablo 4 was a welcome change of vibes and atmosphere for many players — and it sounds like the developers are going to continue this into Diablo 5.
During the Diablo 5 — Forging the Next Era panel, which we watched at BlizzCon 2026 in Anaheim, some of the game's devs spoke openly about the dark and bleak setting that Diablo 5 will have.
"I think that's really the tone, the atmosphere," said John Mueller, senior art director. "We're really doubling down on darkness, and what this means for the art team is we really get to explore all of what we learned from Diablo 4 and expand on it further. You know, that desolation that we're going to see in the world is really the setting for the survivors of this story [in Diablo 5]."
This is something that I'm absolutely here for; Diablo games thrive and are at their bleakest best when they embrace a dark and miserable tone and atmosphere, and help to cement the sense of place Sanctuary has, as well as the overarching richness of the story and narrative.
This doubling down, to the extent of embracing a setting of defeat and one where Sanctuary has fallen, already makes for a compelling starting point that I can't wait for.
However, narrative director Jennifer Hepler went on to add that in the process of "making Sanctuary so, so dark, [and] trying to double down on this darkness of Diablo winning in this apocalyptic setting; we still need to make Sanctuary a place that's worth defending."
So there's a balancing act in play here, then, with the darkness and hopelessness of the setting being somewhat offset by the devs still wanting to make Sanctuary a "place that you want to save."

articles.title: How Togo’s Nihtael Dynasty is helping musicians build more sustainable careers - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nodjigno Pierre Yao Nihtael is well-known in the Togolese music scene, with his Façonné Music label having contributed to the digital distribution of music by more than 50 artists, including Togo Joachin Migos, SCENARIO and IROK.
But though Façonné Music serves as the main platform for Nihtael’s activities in the music sector, he is now taking it a step further with Nihtael Dynasty, which is being developed as a music-industry and creative-economy platform focused on digital distribution, artist development, media strategy, project structuring and market access.
“The objective is not simply to upload music to streaming platforms, but to help artists understand and organise the business around their music so they can build stronger and more sustainable careers,” Nihtael told Disrupt Africa.
Nihtael Dynasty has developed progressively out of his practical work in the Togolese music ecosystem, rather than being launched as a conventional startup on one single date. It is currently being structured into a broader entrepreneurial platform around the services and relationships already developed through Façonné Music.
“The model is collaborative and project-based, working with artists, producers, managers, media contacts, digital-distribution partners and event professionals depending on the needs of each project,” he said.
The main gap is that access to digital distribution has become easier, but professional support around that distribution is still limited for many independent artists in Togo and similar emerging markets.
“An artist may be able to place a song on Spotify, Apple Music or other platforms, but still struggle with metadata, release planning, branding, media relations, audience development, rights awareness, catalogue strategy and international market access,” Nihtael said.
There are distributors, labels, managers and promoters operating in the market, including himself, but Nihtael Dynasty’s approach is to connect several of these functions around the artist, instead of treating distribution as an isolated service.
The response has been encouraging.
“More than 50 artists and projects have already been supported across different stages of development. Demand is increasingly coming not only from artists who want distribution, but also from artists who need help with positioning, media visibility, release strategy and professional development,” said Nihtael.
The core market is Togo, with relationships and project activity extending into the wider West African and African music ecosystem and to international digital platforms.
“The next stage is to strengthen regional connections, particularly across West Africa, while building more direct bridges between African artists, international media, distribution networks and music-industry partners,” Nihtael said.
“The longer-term ambition is for Nihtael Dynasty to become a recognisable support structure for independent African artists seeking both digital access and professional development.”
Revenue is generated through music-industry services and project-based activity, including digital distribution support, artist development, release strategy, media and promotional coordination, and related music-business services.

articles.title: Diablo V prévu pour 2029 : trois classes, monde procédural, Sanctuaire conquis – le point complet sur l'annonce BlizzCon 2026
articles.text:
On pouvait s’en douter : pour les trente ans de la licence, Blizzard allait certainement annoncer quelque chose d’important pour Diablo en 2026. D’aucuns auraient pu penser à une nouvelle extension, la troisième de Diablo IV, après Vessel of Hatred et Lord of Hatred, qui aurait été lancée courant 2027.
Le studio américain avait d’ailleurs déjà commencé les festivités autour de cet anniversaire : une nouvelle classe, le Démoniste, dans Diablo IV, Diablo II: Resurrected, et Diablo Immortal. On a aussi eu droit à une mise à jour (Reign of the Warlock) pour Diablo II: Resurrected, et puis Lord of Hatred, car, après tout, l’extension est sortie en avril dernier.
Mais voilà : Blizzard a décidé d’en faire plus. Après avoir célébré au passage la communauté de Diablo, avec une vidéo retraçant l’histoire de la licence et soulignant le dynamisme des joueurs et des joueuses, on a eu droit à Diablo V. Déjà, diront certains ; après tout, les épisodes précédents étaient bien plus espacés dans le temps.
La cérémonie d’ouverture de la BlizzCon 2026, ce week-end des 12 et 13 septembre, a ainsi confirmé le développement de Diablo V et calé une sortie au printemps 2029. Eh bien, l’ambiance n’est pas à la fête dans ce prochain volet : Sanctuaire est tombé, Diablo a gagné. Comment ? Pourquoi ? On le saura dans presque trois ans.
Qu’est-ce qui change vraiment ?
Le postulat, d’abord. Dans les épisodes précédents, Diablo était la menace finale, le boss que l’on affrontait au bout du périple (ou l’un de ses frères). Cette fois, il a déjà gagné. Installé sur le trône d’Ouestmarche, le seigneur de la Terreur se sert des âmes de Sanctuaire comme d’armes et façonne le monde dès les premières minutes.
Or, ce Sanctuaire n’a plus rien de stable. Dans une longue présentation, l’équipe de développement a détaillé sa vision, appuyée par une bande-annonce, qui n’en montre pas beaucoup (si ce n’est un Tyraël vaincu, qui se fait achever à terre, mais aussi des myriades de suppliciés et des démons partout, ainsi qu’un Diablo surgissant des flammes).
Fini aussi, les villes et les bastions sûrs. Pour survivre, il faudra constituer une caravane d’alliés qui font à la fois office de marchands et de compagnons de route, comme cette ancienne sœur de l’Œil aveugle ou ce gobelin au trésor en quête de sens dans un monde où la cupidité ne rime plus à rien.
Cela ne s’arrête pas là : le monde est généré de façon procédurale, si bien que le terrain, les points d’intérêt, les monstres et les récompenses peuvent changer à chaque retour. Quant au joueur, il incarne un survivant lié de façon mystérieuse à Diablo, en fuite parmi les ruines d’un royaume transformé en avant-poste des Enfers.
Trois classes Diablo V annoncées, dont une inédite, et des items repensés
Côté personnages, trois classes ont été dévoilées. Les chasseurs de démons reviennent avec leurs deux arbalètes, les moines avec leurs arts martiaux, et un profil inédit fait son entrée : les chevaliers de la peste, qui répandent maladie et fléau avant de s’en nourrir pour gagner en puissance. Les deux premières étaient proposées notamment sur Diablo III.
Blizzard prévient qu’il s’agit seulement des premières, d’autres suivront d’ici la sortie.
Le système d’objets évolue par ailleurs. L’équipe de développement déclare ouvertement s’inspirer de Diablo II, sorti en 2000 et resté une référence pour les vétérans et les puristes : comprendre de nouvelles caractéristiques à satisfaire pour pouvoir y prétendre, mais aussi de nouvelles contraintes dans l’espace de stockage à intégrer.
Dans le détail, des objets vont exiger des caractéristiques bien précises pour être équipés. Par ailleurs, les pièces les plus imposantes vont prendre bien plus de place dans l’inventaire. À cela s’ajoute le retour des ensembles d’équipement, et des runes et mots runiques. Là encore, c’est du côté de Diablo II que l’on a choisi de lorgner.
L’artisanat, de son côté, reprend l’approche de l’extension Lord of Hatred de Diablo IV.
Une suite qui arrive rapidement
Quand on pense que quatre ans séparent le premier Diablo du deuxième volet, puis que douze ans ont passé avant de voir Diablo III et encore onze ans avec l’épisode actuel (sans compter les extensions), Diablo V a été révélé rapidement. Cependant, il va encore s’écouler du temps, puisque la sortie n’adviendra que dans trois ans.
Une annonce si tôt rappelle que Diablo reste une machine à cash. Diablo IV, sorti en 2023, a signé le meilleur lancement de l’histoire de Blizzard, avec plus de 666 millions de dollars (environ 575 millions d’euros) engrangés en cinq jours. Et les microtransactions ont été un moteur non négligeable dans le succès commercial du titre.
Certes, la promesse initiale de sortir une extension par an n’a pas été tenue, car, après la sortie du jeu en 2023, on a eu plutôt droit à un rythme d’une sortie tous les dix-huit mois, voire deux ans (Vessel of Hatred est arrivée en octobre 2024 et Lord of Hatred en avril 2026). Le jeu a été alimenté avec des saisons et des classes, cependant.
Par ailleurs, l’annonce de Diablo V ne signe pas l’abandon du titre actuel par Blizzard : ainsi, la classe de l’amazone fera ses débuts dans Diablo IV au cours du premier semestre de 2027, en provenance de Skovos. Qui plus est, une nouvelle saison (l’héritage infernal) arrivera dès le 15 septembre en jeu, qui est un hommage à la licence.
Et puis Diablo IV arrive sur Nintendo Switch 2.
Cela étant dit, Diablo V tient surtout de la déclaration d’intention en l’état : le jeu n’en est qu’aux prémices de son développement, et rien n’a encore été montré en termes de gameplay. Il faudra lever les zones d’ombre, comme le prix et les plateformes. Les fans patienteront avec Diablo IV et la future série animée conçue avec Netflix.

articles.title: Stockholm’s Tandem Health raises €86.5 million to build an AI-native operating system for European healthcare | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Tandem Health, a Stockholm-based HealthTech startup building a complete AI medical assistant for European clinics, has raised €86.49 million ($100 million) in Series B funding,
The round was led by the Scaleup Europe Fund, managed by EQT, with support from existing investors Kinnevik, Northzone, Amino Collective, and Visionaries. In June 2025, the company announced a €42.6 million Series A funding round led by Kinnevik. With the new round, the Swedish company has raised a total of €138.38 million ($160 million).
Lukas Saari, CEO and co-founder of Tandem Health, said, “Europe’s health systems are under real strain and AI presents a real solution. But until now, European care providers have had to depend either on legacy solutions or AI solutions originally built for other markets that were retrofitted for Europe.
“We started Tandem to provide an alternative. Europe should be setting the standard for how AI enters healthcare, not adopting someone else’s. This funding lets us do that, bringing healthcare safely into the AI era, working in tandem with patients, clinicians, systems and nations. That’s how we’re taking care of healthcare.”
Founded in 2023 by Oscar Boldt-Christmas (CCO), Oliver Åstrand (CTO), and Saari, Tandem Health is building the AI-native clinic operating system for European healthcare. Its AI medical assistant supports clinicians throughout the entire patient visit, from documentation to coding to clinical decision support.
According to the company, the current trajectory, with rising healthcare costs, clinician shortages, and an ageing population, is not sustainable. Tandem Health claims to be part of the solution and is building clinically safe, regulatory-grade AI that clinicians can trust.
The company states that it offers a complete AI medical assistant that supports clinicians before, during, and after patient visits. It prepares patient summaries ahead of appointments, provides clinical decision support during consultations, and automatically handles the subsequent documentation and coding.
It highlights that it is the only AI Medical Assistant with an AI scribe, coding assistant, and clinical decision support, each of which is independently certified as a Class IIa medical device under the EU Medical Device Regulation. It is also certified according to ISO 27001, ISO 13485, ISO 42001, C5 in Germany, ENS High in Spain, and HDS in France.
Earlier this year, in January, Tandem Health announced the acquisition of Dutch AI medical scribe Juvoly to scale clinician-first AI documentation across Europe.
The company, citing peer-reviewed research, reported that clinicians using Tandem witnessed a 29% reduction in time spent on admin, a 30% improvement in job satisfaction and a 30% reduction in administrative stress.
Nils Petter Nygaard, Managing Director at EQT and Scaleup Europe Fund, said, “Europe’s healthcare system is composed of a myriad of complexities, including fragmented regulatory regimes and highly varied care models. Tandem is one of the few healthcare technology companies to demonstrate it can scale in a pan-European way, already supporting more than 10,000 care organisations with AI that reduces administrative burden and frees up clinicians’ time for higher-impact work. We believe Tandem has the potential to become the foundational AI layer for European healthcare over the coming decades.”
The Scaleup Europe Fund, targeting €5 billion, was initiated by the European Commission and is managed by EQT. It brings together public and private capital to back ambitious European technology companies at scale, helping them grow while strengthening Europe’s technology ecosystem and competitiveness.
Tandem Health plans to use this capital to further accelerate its position as the AI partner of Europe’s leading care providers. It aims to continue doubling down across markets and to expand the clinician-led team, which already comprises 75+ in-house clinicians developing and delivering AI solutions.
It also intends to evolve from an AI medical assistant to an AI-native clinic operating system that also manages patient flows and enables agents that solve additional clinical tasks.
Since its inception, Tandem has established offices in 14 European markets and has been adopted by more than 10,000 care organisations. These include some of Europe’s largest care providers, such as Ramsay Santé, Humanitas, and the NHS.

articles.title: Piscine, running, vélo : ce casque open-ear avec MP3 passe à 42,99€
articles.text:
Sous l’eau, le Bluetooth atteint vite ses limites, ce qui rend la mémoire intégrée particulièrement utile pour nager en musique. À 42,99 € chez Amazon, ce casque à conduction osseuse combine IPX8 et lecteur MP3 8 Go dans une formule pensée pour la piscine comme pour les entraînements à terre.
Ce modèle se présente comme un casque sportif à oreilles libres, avec conduction osseuse, certification IPX8 et lecteur MP3 intégré de 8 Go. Son intérêt est surtout concret pour la natation : le mode MP3 permet d’écouter des fichiers stockés localement lorsque la liaison Bluetooth n’est pas exploitable sous l’eau. Hors de la piscine, le Bluetooth 6.0 et le micro anti-vent sont annoncés pour la course, le vélo ou les appels, deux caractéristiques à considérer comme des données de fiche produit plutôt que comme des performances mesurées.
À ce niveau de prix, l’offre à 42,99 € chez Amazon vise donc surtout les sportifs qui veulent essayer la conduction osseuse sans s’orienter d’emblée vers une référence plus coûteuse.
Le casque à conduction osseuse IPX8 avec MP3 8 Go est proposé à 42,99 € chez Amazon, alors que le prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours indiqué pour cette offre est de 129,99 €.
Pourquoi choisir ce casque à conduction osseuse IPX8 ?
- Un mode MP3 pertinent en piscine : La mémoire intégrée de 8 Go permet de charger de la musique avant la séance. C’est essentiel sous l’eau, puisque le Bluetooth ne traverse pas correctement la surface et ne remplace pas un stockage local pendant les longueurs.
- Des oreilles qui restent dégagées : La conduction osseuse transmet le son sans obstruer le conduit auditif. Ce format peut aider à conserver davantage de perception de l’environnement à la course ou à vélo, sans dispenser de rester attentif à la circulation.
- Un ticket d’entrée nettement abaissé : À 42,99 €, le prix actuel se situe 87 € sous le prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours communiqué pour l’offre, fixé à 129,99 €. Pour découvrir le principe avant d’investir davantage, l’écart de prix est l’argument le plus concret.
Un format surtout intéressant quand le téléphone doit rester au vestiaire
En piscine, ce casque prend son sens grâce au couple IPX8 et MP3 8 Go : vous préparez vos morceaux à l’avance et il fonctionne sans dépendre du smartphone pendant la nage. À terre, il redevient un casque Bluetooth open-ear pour la course ou le vélo, sans boucher les oreilles. Clubic rappelle dans notre comparatif des meilleurs écouteurs Bluetooth pour le sport que maintien, confort et résistance aux éléments comptent autant que la qualité audio pendant l’entraînement. Ce modèle s’adresse donc davantage au nageur occasionnel ou au sportif polyvalent qu’à l’audiophile recherchant une écoute très isolante.
Un prix bas, avec moins de recul qu’une référence bien documentée
Cette offre mise d’abord sur son tarif et sa double utilisation MP3/Bluetooth, mais elle ne bénéficie pas du même recul éditorial que des références déjà testées en détail. Les modèles de marques plus établies restent plus rassurants pour un usage intensif, tandis que ce casque paraît surtout cohérent pour tester le format à moindre coût.
✅ Les points forts
- Certification IPX8 annoncée pour un usage en natation
- Lecteur MP3 intégré avec 8 Go de stockage
- Format open-ear à conduction osseuse, sans embout dans le conduit auditif
- Bluetooth pour les usages sportifs hors de l’eau
❌ Les limites
- Le Bluetooth n’est pas utilisable sous l’eau : il faut passer par les fichiers MP3 stockés localement
- Qualité sonore et performances du micro non documentées par un test indépendant fourni avec l’offre
- Peu de recul sur la fiabilité à long terme et le service après-vente de ce modèle
Si ce compromis entre natation en MP3 et usage Bluetooth à terre vous convient, vérifiez que ce casque est toujours affiché à 42,99 € chez Amazon avant de commander.
À 42,99 €, ce casque est surtout intéressant parce qu’il couvre deux contextes que les écouteurs classiques gèrent mal ensemble. Le stockage MP3 répond au problème de la connexion sous l’eau, tandis que la conception open-ear et le Bluetooth prennent davantage de sens pour courir ou pédaler. Pour un nageur occasionnel, un triathlète amateur ou un sportif curieux de la conduction osseuse, la proposition est facile à comprendre.
Il faut toutefois garder le prix en perspective avec le manque de recul sur ce modèle précis. Les performances audio, le micro anti-vent et la durabilité ne sont pas documentés ici par des mesures indépendantes, et la conduction osseuse n’est pas le format à privilégier si vous recherchez des basses puissantes ou une forte isolation. Les utilisateurs intensifs auront intérêt à comparer avec des références mieux documentées ; ceux qui veulent surtout écouter leur musique en piscine sans dépasser une cinquantaine d’euros peuvent y voir un compromis cohérent.
